newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-LILLEY TAMES HURRICANES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LILLEY TAMES HURRICANES.

text.p: Canterbury Crusaders, last season's Super 12 wooden spoonists, made an encouraging start to their 1997 campaign with a 19-17 win over the Wellington Hurricanes at Lancaster Park on Friday.

The Crusaders were outscored two tries to one, but emerged victorious thanks to four penalties from the boot of fullback Daryl Lilley who made the most of a 16-2 penalty count against Wellington, beaten 23-18 at home by Waikato in their opening game last week.
Lilley put over three first half penalties, two of them following high tackles by flankers Filo Tiatia and Potu Leavasa, to give the Crusaders a 9-3 half-time lead.
The Crusaders then took charge of the game a minute after the break when winger James Kerr latched on to a Lilley kick to touch down in the corner.
The Hurricanes came back with a solid try to Alama Ieremia and an opportunist try by classy halfback Jon Preston, but by then the Crusaders' forwards were in control.

Canterbury Crusaders - Daryl Lilley, James Kerr, Tabai Matson, Paula Bale, Mark Mayerhofler; Leon MacDonald, Justin Marshall; Steve Surridge, Scott Robertson, Steve Lancaster, Mark Weedon, Todd Blackadder (captain), Con Barrell, Mark Hammett, Kevin Nepia.

Wellington Hurricanes - Christian Cullen; Tana Umaga, Alama Ieremia, Roger Randle, Jason O'Halloran; Stephen Bachop, Jon Preston; Karl Williams, Filo Tiatia, Mike Russell, Mark Cooksley, Potu Leavasa, Phil Coffin, Norm Hewitt, Mark Allen (captain).
